raw_response:
I'm 32, farming these 18 mu for 10 years now since I married into this village. My husband works construction in Handan when there's no urgent farm work, so it's mostly me and my mother-in-law handling the day-to-day, plus our two school-age kids helping on weekends. I only finished primary school, so I don't know much about those technical calculations — I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

Our main field is 10 mu of wheat-maize double crop. That's our rice bowl, can't mess with it. The wheat went in last October like always. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — about 50 kg a bag — and come March when the wheat turns green I'll spread another half-bag of urea. My neighbor Aunt Li cut her fertilizer last year and said it was okay, but I'm too scared to try. If my wheat yields drop, where do I find money for the children's school fees? Better to put a bit more, even if it wastes some money. I'll irrigate three times: once when it wakes up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water from the well costs electricity, but you can't skip it.

For maize, we plant right after wheat harvest around June 10th-15th. We hire the combine for wheat, then rush to get maize in the ground within a few days. I buy hybrid seed — saved seed doesn't grow well for maize, I learned that the hard way years ago. I put one bag of compound fertilizer and a bit of urea in the holes at planting, then topdress with another half-bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations: one after planting if it's dry, one at the big trumpet stage.

I keep 4 mu of cabbage because the vegetable buyer comes right to our village. I plant in late March and harvest by mid-June before maize gets busy. Cabbage eats fertilizer — I put down chicken manure and about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then another bag split between rosette stage and heading. It's more work but the profit is better than grain, and we need cash.

Eggplant is on 3 mu. We start seedlings in March in the small greenhouse and transplant in early May. My mother-in-law is good at tending eggplant — she knows when to water and when to hold back. It needs spraying for insects and mildew. We sell at the county vegetable market on Sundays when my husband can drive us.

I also keep 1 mu of stevia. The factory buyer comes every year and the price is steady, not like vegetables that jump up and down. Plant in April, cut the leaves twice in summer. Not much work, just some fertilizer at planting and weeding. We hire two people to help with the cutting because it's fast and you can't wait once it's ready.

We only hire labor for wheat combining and if we're behind on maize planting. The cabbage, eggplant, and stevia we handle ourselves — can't afford to hire for everything. I keep some cash in hand always, never spend the last few thousand yuan. A bad year or someone getting sick and you're finished if you have no savings.
